```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(fedmatch)   # clean_strings()
```

## The problem

In World of Warcraft raiding, the Augmentation Evoker is a support specialization whose main job is buffing other players. Its key buff, *Prescience*, should go to whichever players will deal the most damage during each burst window (each cast of *Ebon Might*). With up to three Augmentation Evokers in a raid, each one needs a list of who to buff and when, and two Evokers should never buff the same player at overlapping times.

Players data was collected from warcraft logs API and then damage in each window as calculated.

This notebook automates the assignments. It takes a ranking of players by expected damage in each window, plus a schedule of Prescience casts, and assigns a target to every cast for all three Evokers without overlaps.

This script allowed us to quickly evaluate performance and allocate accordingly.

## Data

Two inputs:

- **`output.csv`**: For each burst window (`EM1`–`EM7`), a list of players ranked by expected damage, best first. - Taken from warcraftlogs and processed for damage windows.
- **`EM_timings_New.csv`**: One row per Prescience cast, with the cast time, expiration time, the burst window it falls in, and an assignment priority (1 = fill first).

```{r load-data}
damage_data_original = read.csv('data/output.csv')
em_timings = read.csv('data/EM_timings_New.csv')
```


Fix names

```{r clean-names}
damage_data = damage_data_original
j = 1
for(j in 1:length(damage_data$X)){
  damage_data$X1[j] = str_to_title(clean_strings(str_split(damage_data$X1[j], ',')[[1]][1]))
  damage_data$X2[j] = str_to_title(clean_strings(str_split(damage_data$X2[j], ',')[[1]][1]))
  damage_data$X3[j] = str_to_title(clean_strings(str_split(damage_data$X3[j], ',')[[1]][1]))
  damage_data$X4[j] = str_to_title(clean_strings(str_split(damage_data$X4[j], ',')[[1]][1]))
  damage_data$X5[j] = str_to_title(clean_strings(str_split(damage_data$X5[j], ',')[[1]][1]))
  damage_data$X6[j] = str_to_title(clean_strings(str_split(damage_data$X6[j], ',')[[1]][1]))
  damage_data$X7[j] = str_to_title(clean_strings(str_split(damage_data$X7[j], ',')[[1]][1]))
}

colnames(damage_data) = c('PlayerNum', 'EM1', 'EM2', 'EM3','EM4', 'EM5', 'EM6', 'EM7')
head(damage_data)
```

## Method

Assignment is greedy. For each Prescience cast, the function:

1. Finds every existing assignment (for any of the three Evokers) whose buff would overlap this cast's duration.
2. Removes those players from this window's ranked list, along with anyone excluded entirely. This allows evokers to maintain current targets.
3. Assigns the highest-ranked player left.

Windows beyond the last ranked column fall back to the `EM7` ranking.

```{r target-picker}
TargetPickerFunction = function(EMWindow, CastTime, ExpirationTime, CurrentPrescienceAssigments, InputData, RemovedPlayers){

  # Ranking column for this burst window; windows past the last column use EM7
  EMColumn = paste0('EM', min(EMWindow, 7))

  PossibleConflicts = CurrentPrescienceAssigments %>%
    filter(Prescience_expiration_time >= CastTime & Prescience_Cast_time <= CastTime | Prescience_Cast_time <= ExpirationTime & Prescience_Cast_time >= CastTime)
  ConflictList1 = PossibleConflicts$Augvoker_Set_1
  ConflictList2 = PossibleConflicts$Augvoker_Set_2
  ConflictList3 = PossibleConflicts$Augvoker_Set_3

  Filtered_Target_List = InputData %>%
    filter(.data[[EMColumn]] %in% ConflictList1 == "FALSE")
  Filtered_Target_List = Filtered_Target_List %>%
    filter(.data[[EMColumn]] %in% ConflictList2 == "FALSE")
  Filtered_Target_List = Filtered_Target_List %>%
    filter(.data[[EMColumn]] %in% ConflictList3 == "FALSE")
  Filtered_Target_List = Filtered_Target_List %>%
    filter(.data[[EMColumn]] %in% RemovedPlayers == "FALSE")

  PrescienceTarget = Filtered_Target_List[[EMColumn]][1]
  return(PrescienceTarget)
}
```

Assignments are filled one Evoker at a time. Within each Evoker, higher-priority casts are filled first so they get first pick of the top players.

```{r assign}
DoNotInclude = c('Baldevoker')   # players never assigned Prescience

for(SetColumn in c('Augvoker_Set_1', 'Augvoker_Set_2', 'Augvoker_Set_3')){
  for(Priority in 1:5){
    PriorityList = em_timings %>%
      filter(Assignment_Priority == Priority)

    for(j in seq_len(nrow(PriorityList))){
      em_timings[[SetColumn]][PriorityList$Prescience_Number[j]] = TargetPickerFunction(PriorityList$Timing_window[j], PriorityList$Prescience_Cast_time[j], PriorityList$Prescience_expiration_time[j], em_timings, damage_data, DoNotInclude)
    }
  }
}

em_timings
```


## Output

The final assignments are written out as text strings formatted for the Method Raid Tools Note, so the raid leader can paste them straight in.

```{r export}
em_timings.finished = em_timings %>%
  mutate(Augvoker_Set_1 = paste0(Augvoker_Set_1, ' ')) %>%
  mutate(Augvoker_Set_2 = paste0(Augvoker_Set_2, ' ')) %>%
  mutate(Augvoker_Set_3 = paste0(Augvoker_Set_3, ' '))

# TODO: In the original, Auglist2 repeats Set_1 and Auglist3/Auglist4 both use
# Set_2, so Set_3 never reaches the export. Confirm which set belongs in each
# string and update the column used in each loop below.

Auglist1 = "startAug AugName("
j = 1
for(j in 1:length(em_timings.finished$Augvoker_Set_1)){
  Auglist1 = paste0(Auglist1, em_timings.finished$Augvoker_Set_1[j])
}
Auglist1 = paste0(Auglist1, ') ')

Auglist2 = " AugName ("
j = 1
for(j in 1:length(em_timings.finished$Augvoker_Set_1)){
  Auglist2 = paste0(Auglist2, em_timings.finished$Augvoker_Set_1[j])
}
Auglist2 = paste0(Auglist2, ')endAug')

Auglist3 = "Augvoker Start:"
j = 1
for(j in 1:length(em_timings.finished$Augvoker_Set_2)){
  Auglist3 = paste0(Auglist3, em_timings.finished$Augvoker_Set_2[j])
}

Auglist4 = "Augvoker Start:"
j = 1
for(j in 1:length(em_timings.finished$Augvoker_Set_2)){
  Auglist4 = paste0(Auglist4, em_timings.finished$Augvoker_Set_2[j])
}

AugFinal = data.frame(Auglist1, Auglist2, Auglist3, Auglist4)
write.csv(AugFinal, file = "AugAssignments.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Limitations and possible extensions

This worked incredibly well. The important part was that augvokers pressed their button during the correct window for refreshing - if they were off on their timing, then desyncs happen. However, when all players played well - the results were excellent.
